newsitem.title: CHINA: China central bank governor defends rate cuts.
newsitem.headline: China central bank governor defends rate cuts.

text.p: China's central bank governor Dai Xianglong defended on Tuesday two interest rate cuts this year, saying they were not a sign the bank would relax monetary policy.
Speaking to an international business conference, he also said retail prices would rise by about 7.0 percent this year and annual economic growth would be about 10 percent.

"The two interest rate cuts were made under the condition of falling prices," said Dai, head of the People's Bank of China. "Therefore one cannot draw the conclusion that the central bank will relax monetary policy."
Dai said that monetary policy over the current five-year plan (1996-2000) should be neither too lax nor too tight.
"A relatively tight monetary policy should continue to be pursued," he said. "Control of inflation should be regarded as the primary task in macro-economic adjustment...in the financial sector."

China cut interest rates in May and August in response to falling inflation. Retail price inflation was a year-on-year 5.8 percent in August. China had set a target of 10 percent inflation for 1996, down from 14.8 percent last year.
